title: Malaysia Airlines says customers may be affected by Amadeus breach
text:
Malaysia Airlines says customers may be affected by Amadeus breach Sunday 01 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Aviation Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google SINGAPORE (Nov 1): Malaysia Airlines said on Sunday that some customer information may have been affected by a cybersecurity incident involving Amadeus, its reservation-technology provider.
 The airline joins Cathay Pacific Airways, Japan Airlines, South Korea's Asiana Airlines and others in recent days that have reported customer data was compromised in the Amadeus breach.
 Malaysia's flag carrier said in a statement that the incident may have affected information processed between August 2023 and September this year.
 The airline said it is working with Amadeus and relevant parties to investigate the incident and assess its impact.
 Malaysia Airlines said its IT systems were not breached and there was no evidence that financial information had been accessed.
 The airline encouraged customers to remain vigilant against suspicious or unsolicited communications, particularly those requesting personal or financial information.
 Amadeus said it had become aware of a vulnerability affecting a travel ​booking display ​environment but ⁠ did not respond to a question on how many customers' data ​were affected.
 In recent days Cathay Pacific and Japan Airlines reported that the breach had affected data involving 53,000 bookings and 92,000 customers, respectively.
